full_judgment:
2. Daulat Ahmed and his two brothers namely. Karimul Haque and Nasimul Haque as petitioners instituted Misc. Case No. 1 of 1992 in the Court of the learned Assistant Judge, Ramgonj seeking pre-emption of the case land under section 96 of the aforesaid Act against opposite party No. 1 namely, Md. Mosharraf Hossain as pre-emptee and opposite party No. 2 Sree Partha Banik as the vendor contending, inter alia, that the petitioners were tenants in respect of 97 decimals of land of Khatian No. 4 Satarpara Mouza as described in schedule ''Ka'' to the pre-emption petition. Afterwards they also purchased. 7-1/2 acres of land from one Abul Kalam and 9.5 acres from Md Sharifullah through registered kabala dated 17-1-87 from the same khatian No. 4 and thus became co-sharer of the holding. 

 10. Mr. Md Ozair Farooq, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners, strongly supported the judgment and order passed by the Assistant Judge, Ramgonj and very virulently assailed those of the appellate Court. Mr. Farooq submits: a) that the District Judge erred in holding that the disputed deed is a "deed of exchange" and nota deed of sale b) that the District Judge also erred in holding that the PWs indirectly or by implication admitted that opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 in between them had an exchange in respect of ''Ka'' and ''Kha'' schedule land by using, the expression “জেরার জবাবে পরোক্ষভাবে হইলেও স্বীকার করিয়াছে যে ১/২ নং প্রতিপক্ষ আপীলগন নং ‘ক’ তপছিল বর্ণিত ভূমি এওয়াজ বিনিময় করিয়াছে।   inasmuch as no such indirect admission can be inferred from the cross-examination of the PWs on record. In order to put emphasis and find out the fallacy that an error has been committed by the court of appeal below he has referred to the deposition of PWs Haran Chandra Sil who stated that opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 and the land in schedule ''Ka'' and ''Kha'' respectively are known to him and he came to know from different sources that opposite party No. 2 Sree Partha Banik sold out the ''Ka’ schedule land to opposite party No. 1 Md. Mosharraf Hossain. Mr Farooq also referred to the deposition of PW 4 Md Hanif who also corroborated PW 2 Haran Chandra Sil by stating that he heard before that Sree Partha Banik sold out the disputed property to Md Mosharraf Hossain, then said that they made an ewaj and used the expression —“আগে শুনিয়াছে খরিদ বিক্রয় করে পরে শুনিয়াছি এওয়াজ বদল হইয়াছে। c) Mr Farooq also submits that the court of appeal below committed an error of law by ignoring the contradiction in the deposition of OPWs 1 and 2 in respect of possession of ''Kha'' schedule land by opposite party No. 1 Sree Partha Banik and without adverting to the finding of facts as regards lack of delivery of possession of ''kha'' schedule land to the opposite party No. 2 pursuant to the alleged exchange the court of appeal below reversed the decision of the trial Court and in so doing MrFarooq referred to the deposition of DW 2 Sree Partha Banik who in his cross-examination stated that “জমি না মাপিয়া দখল দিয়াছিল” although from schedule ''Kha'' it is clear that the quantum of land in that schedule is 2.92 acres and out of that only a small fraction of 2-1/2 acres was exchanged. Mr Farooq also referred to the deposition of PW 1 namely, opposite party No. 1 Md. Mosharraf Hossain who stated that the ''Kha'' schedule land which is to the west of his house is a high land situated by the side of Khal and that the distance between la'' and Kha'' schedule land is one mile and the two schedules form part of 2 (two) different Pourashavas. He further stated that his residence is in Mouza Nandanpur but he could not recollect the plot number and the Khatian of his house and he could not file any paper and document in support of his contention that the said house belonged to him; that the ''Kha'' schedule land is adjacent to his house and the same is high land (vhiti) by the side of a canal and the said fact is also corroborated by DW 2 Partha Banik stating “খ” তপছিল ভূমি খাল সংলগ্ন ভিটি জমি”।
